properties.statement:
`add_change_event`'s `change_type` ENUM HAS NO VALUE FOR A DEFECT FOUND IN THE FIELD, SO RECORDING ONE FORCES A SMALL FICTION. Hit here on 2026-08-08 recording the DUPLICATES/merge fix. The enum is `requirement_creep | new_feature | test_failure_fix | performance_optimization | refactor | scope_change | constraint_change | environment_change | deprecation | resync | baseline_established`. The change being recorded was a defect REPORTED BY A USER of the built system — dev_storyflow's fleet — and diagnosed here. No test had failed; there was no test at all, which was part of the defect. `test_failure_fix` was chosen as the nearest fit and the event NAME says explicitly that no failing test existed, so the ledger is not silently wrong — but the structured field still says something untrue and only the prose corrects it. WHY THIS IS NOT PEDANTRY, and the schema itself makes the argument: `baseline_established` exists precisely because forcing a record-only change through `refactor`/`test_failure_fix` 'writes a fiction into the ledger that exists to prevent fiction' (its own description, BL-157). That reasoning applies unchanged one category along. THE DISTINCTION WORTH KEEPING if a value is added: a defect found by a CHECK and a defect found by a USER are different provenance for the same repair, and reflow2 already cares about that difference everywhere else — `set_provenance` grades authored/inferred/reconciled, and `cap:independent-evidence` refuses to let evidence a value was fitted to count as validating it. FIX SHAPE: add `defect_fix` (or `field_report_fix`); or, smaller, let the event carry a `reported_by`/`found_by` property so the how-it-was-found is structured rather than narrated. NOTE THE MILD IRONY, recorded because it is the same class the fleet reported six times: this is a structured field that answers a slightly different question than the writer's, and the only thing preserving the truth is prose beside it — which is exactly fact:defect-verification-evidence-is-prose-so-passing-can-contradict-itself, one node type over.

═══ CORROBORATED BY A SECOND PROJECT, AND THE COUNT IS NOW FIVE (2026-08-15) ═══

This stopped being one maintainer's papercut. Alex's Grok 4.6 session, 2026-08-14, hit it INDEPENDENTLY on a different project with no knowledge of this node, and filed it as its number-one issue (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md, item 1): it tried `bugfix`, was refused, and settled on `test_failure_fix` for a client cache leaving a derived flag stale — 'The enum forces a lie.' It reached the same fix shape unprompted: 'a type for \"implementation defect against existing intent\" (or document that test_failure_fix is that bucket).' TWO AGENTS ON TWO PROJECTS DERIVING THE SAME MISSING VALUE FROM THE SAME ELEVEN OPTIONS is the evidence this node lacked on 2026-08-08, when it was a single observation.

AND THE LEDGER ALREADY CONTAINS THE PATTERN, which nobody had counted: (1) `chg:duplicate-merge-needs-a-human-20260808` — `test_failure_fix`, no test existed; (2) `chg:accept-acb06c45b63a7b6d` — `test_failure_fix`, whose own name says 'recorded under test_failure_fix because the enum has no value meaning \"the code was wrong\"'; (3) `chg:arrival-delta-decided` — `scope_change` 'used as least-wrong: nothing in the enum means \"an open question was settled\"'; (4) Alex's session, 2026-08-14; (5) `chg:change-type-gap-corroborated-by-a-second-project` — THIS VERY EDIT, filed under `resync` because nothing means 'the design's knowledge of an unchanged fact improved'. FIVE FORCED CHOICES, and reflow2's own ledger is where four of them are written down.

⭐ THE SHARPENING, and it changes the fix: (3) and (5) are NOT the missing defect value. 'An open question was settled' and 'what we know moved while the thing did not' are two further meanings with no home. So the enum is short by at least three, which makes 'add `defect_fix`' the wrong shape of answer — it fixes the loudest instance and leaves the pattern. THE PATTERN IS THAT `change_type` CONFLATES TWO AXES: what happened to the SYSTEM (new_feature, refactor, deprecation) and what happened to the RECORD (baseline_established, resync, and the three missing ones). `baseline_established`'s own doc comment already says so — 'the odd one out, and deliberately so. Every other variant answers why the thing changed; this one says the thing did not change and only the design's knowledge of it did' — which names the second axis while leaving it with exactly one member and a reservation preventing its use. NOT ESTABLISHED: whether splitting the axes (a `subject: system|record` alongside a narrower type) is better than adding three values; that is a schema question and Anthony's call. NOTE the enum values are NOT counted by the version stamp, so adding values is not a schema break — established when the `medium` enum question was dissolved.
